hook: SCP-2118 is a young girl who talks mostly in sign language, for a reason the first interview lets her explain in her own words. The article is short, built around three interviews, and each one hurts in a different way. It involves the deaths of children, including murder, and the sounds of their dying moments.
whyItMatters: Its effect turns the familiar idea of hearing the dead into a cruelty for everyone involved: the bereaved parent, the people watching and above all the child who cannot make it stop. The bracketed sign language running alongside the borrowed voice gives each log two speakers at once, and that split is the article's main technique. It is a strong example of an anomaly that works as a moral test for the people around it rather than a threat to the world.
thingsToNotice:
The first interview sets up her guilt: she assumes she did something bad, apologises constantly, and says she once glued her mouth shut and ended up in hospital. The second turns the effect into an accusation, first exposing D-3498 through his three-year-old daughter's screams and choking, then unexpectedly catching one of the agents in the room, as a boy of about eight complains of cold and pain while SCP-2118 signs to ask why; that agent ends up under police investigation.

The last log is the saddest. Researcher Anselman, not even assigned to her, wakes her at night to hear his son Dewey, and the two voices split: the boy asks what happens after death and tells his dad he loves him, while the girl signs that she cannot become him for anyone and hates being here. Watch the ending, where she presses her forehead to the glass long after he has been led away.
